subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw support explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files in the bundled `bootstrap-extra-files` hook, and should the active fix use exact `sessions[sessionKey]` config or a narrower global custom-file contract?
rationale: The source-level fix is clear, but it changes which operator-configured files can enter deterministic startup context and the linked PR adds a new exact-session config surface, so maintainer intent is required for the product/security contract.

options.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
options.body: Allow custom basenames only when explicitly configured and still protected by workspace containment, size budgets, diagnostics, deterministic ordering, and session filtering, then repair or rebase the linked PR.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Leave the bundled hook restricted to known bootstrap filenames and route arbitrary context files to a separate plugin or future context API.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context Design
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose a larger context-files, session-filtering, or capability-discovery API that covers this need.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
recommendation.body: Allow custom basenames only when explicitly configured and still protected by workspace containment, size budgets, diagnostics, deterministic ordering, and session filtering, then repair or rebase the linked PR.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest adjacent history on boundary-safe bootstrap file reads and appears in the original hook history, making them the best available owner for the contract choice.
